Athabasca Falls, Canada 🇨🇦

Nestled within Jasper National Park, Athabasca Falls is one of the park’s most powerful natural wonders. Though only 24 meters high, its strength lies not in height—but in raw, unrelenting force. A massive volume of glacier-fed water funnels through a narrow limestone canyon, producing a thunderous roar and a perpetual mist that hangs in the air.

Fed by meltwater from the Columbia Icefield, the Athabasca River carries a vivid turquoise hue. Over millennia, this relentless flow has carved deep potholes, smoothed rugged canyons, and shaped dramatic rock walls—nature’s own testament to the power of erosion. Well-kept trails and secure viewpoints let visitors feel the falls’ energy up close, safely and immersively.
